diagnostic_examples.overview: Complete end-to-end examples demonstrating the SRE Diagnostics workflow for common incident scenarios. Each example shows the full investigation process from symptom identification through root cause analysis to resolution.

example.name: memory_leak_oomkill
example.title: Memory Leak Causing OOMKilled Pods
example.scenario: Payment service pods are crashing every 2-3 hours with OOMKilled status. Error rate spikes to 15% during crashes. Users report intermittent payment failures.

phase_1_instana.title: Phase 1: Instana Analysis

step.findings: - 8 incidents in last 24 hours - All related to payment-service - Pattern: incidents every 2-3 hours - Each incident lasts 5-10 minutes
- Error rate spikes from 0.1% to 15% during incidents - P99 latency increases from 500ms to 8000ms - Call volume normal (no traffic spike)

step.tool_use:
<use_mcp_tool> <server_name>instana</server_name> <tool_name>analyze_infrastructure</tool_name> <arguments> { "intent": "JVM heap usage for payment service", "entity": "jvm" } </arguments> </use_mcp_tool>
<!-- Then use returned schema --> <use_mcp_tool> <server_name>instana</server_name> <tool_name>analyze_infrastructure</tool_name> <arguments> { "selections": { "entity_type": "jvmRuntimePlatform", "metrics": ["jvm.heap.used", "jvm.heap.maxSize", "jvm.gc.minorTime"], "aggregation": "max", "filters": [ {"name": "service.name", "value": "payment-service"} ], "timeRange": "24h" } } </arguments> </use_mcp_tool>
step.findings: - Heap usage shows sawtooth pattern - Heap grows from 500MB to 1.9GB over 2-3 hours - Sudden drop to 200MB (pod restart) - Pattern repeats consistently - GC pause times increase before crashes

phase_1_instana.hypothesis_formed: Memory leak in payment-service causing heap exhaustion and OOMKills

phase_2_openshift.title: Phase 2: OpenShift Investigation

step.output: NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE payment-service-7d8f9c-xk2lp 1/1 Running 8 24h payment-service-7d8f9c-mn4pq 1/1 Running 7 24h payment-service-7d8f9c-zt9wx 1/1 Running 8 24h
step.findings: - All 3 pods have 7-8 restarts in 24 hours - Confirms 2-3 hour restart pattern

step.key_findings:
Events: Type Reason Age Message ---- ------ ---- ------- Normal Killing 2h ago Stopping container payment-service Warning BackOff 2h ago Back-off restarting failed container Normal Pulled 2h ago Container image pulled Normal Created 2h ago Created container payment-service Normal Started 2h ago Started container payment-service
Last State: Terminated Reason: OOMKilled Exit Code: 137 Started: 2h ago Finished: 2h ago
step.findings: - Exit Code 137 confirms OOMKilled - Kubernetes killed container due to memory limit

step.command: <execute_command> <command>oc get pod payment-service-7d8f9c-xk2lp -n production -o yaml | grep -A 5 resources</command> </execute_command>
step.output: resources: limits: cpu: "2" memory: 2Gi requests: cpu: "1" memory: 1Gi
step.findings: - Memory limit: 2Gi - Heap reaching limit before OOMKill - Limit was adequate for previous versions

step.key_log_entries: 2026-03-15 14:25:29.847 ERROR OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space 2026-03-15 14:25:29.848 ERROR at java.util.HashMap.resize(HashMap.java:704) 2026-03-15 14:25:29.849 ERROR at com.example.UserSessionCache.put(UserSessionCache.java:45)
step.findings: - OutOfMemoryError in UserSessionCache - HashMap.resize() indicates growing collection - Points to specific code location

phase_2_openshift.correlation: OpenShift findings correlate with Instana: - OOMKill timing matches error spikes in Instana - Heap exhaustion pattern matches infrastructure metrics - 2-3 hour cycle consistent across both sources

phase_3_code_analysis.title: Phase 3: Code Analysis

step.issues_identified: 1. Unbounded HashMap - no size limit 2. No eviction policy - entries never removed 3. Static field - shared across all requests 4. No time-based expiration 5. Each UserSession ~2KB, accumulates indefinitely

step.findings:
abc123d Add UserSessionCache for performance improvement (2 days ago)
Cache added in recent deployment, explains timing of incidents

REVISION CHANGE-CAUSE 1 Initial deployment 2 Version 2.2.0 - stable 3 Version 2.3.0 - added UserSessionCache (2 days ago)
Incidents started after v2.3.0 deployment

phase_3_code_analysis.root_cause_confirmed: Unbounded HashMap in UserSessionCache accumulates user sessions without eviction, causing memory leak. After ~900,000 unique logins (2-3 hours at current traffic), heap exhausts and pod is OOMKilled.

immediate_fix.description: Replace HashMap with Guava Cache with eviction policy
immediate_fix.code_change:

<diff>

        cache.put(userId, session);
    }

        return cache.get(userId);

    private static final Cache<String, UserSession> cache = CacheBuilder.newBuilder()
        .maximumSize(10000)
        .expireAfterWrite(1, TimeUnit.HOURS)

        .recordStats()
        .build();

        cache.put(userId, session);

resolution.verification: - Deploy fix as v2.3.1 - Monitor heap usage for 6 hours - Confirm no pod restarts - Verify stable memory at ~45% of limit

rca_report.summary: Payment service experienced recurring outages due to memory leak in UserSessionCache. Unbounded HashMap accumulated user sessions without eviction, causing OOMKills every 2-3 hours. Fixed by implementing cache eviction policy with size and time limits.

example.name: database_connection_pool_exhaustion
example.title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
example.scenario: Order API experiencing intermittent timeouts and "Connection timeout" errors. Latency spikes during peak hours. Database appears healthy.

phase_1_instana.title: Phase 1: Instana Analysis

step.findings: - "Connection timeout" errors in traces - Errors correlate with high request volume - Latency P99 increases from 200ms to 15,000ms - Database query times normal (50-100ms)
- Most time spent waiting for database connection - Actual query execution fast once connection obtained - "Timeout waiting for connection from pool" messages

phase_1_instana.hypothesis_formed: Connection pool exhaustion causing requests to wait for available connections

step.action: Check pod logs during high load
step.findings: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms Active connections: 20, Idle connections: 0, Waiting threads: 45

spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size: 20 spring.datasource.hikari.minimum-idle: 5
Pool size of 20 insufficient for load (100+ concurrent requests)

phase_3_code_analysis.title: Phase 3: Code Analysis

step.findings: No connection leaks found - all connections properly closed
- Each request uses 1 connection - Connections held for ~100ms average - No long-running transactions - Pool size (20) too small for concurrent load (100+ requests)

phase_3_code_analysis.root_cause_confirmed: Connection pool size (20) insufficient for peak load. With 100+ concurrent requests and 100ms average connection hold time, pool exhausts and requests timeout waiting for connections.

immediate_fix.description: Increase connection pool size based on load analysis
immediate_fix.calculation: Peak concurrent requests: 120 Average connection hold time: 100ms Required pool size: 120 * 0.1 = 12 (minimum) Recommended: 50 (with buffer for spikes)
immediate_fix.config_change: <apply_diff> <path>config/application.yml</path> <diff> <<<<<<< SEARCH :start_line:15 ------- spring: datasource: hikari: maximum-pool-size: 20 minimum-idle: 5 ======= spring: datasource: hikari: maximum-pool-size: 50 minimum-idle: 10 connection-timeout: 30000 idle-timeout: 600000 max-lifetime: 1800000 >>>>>>> REPLACE </diff> </apply_diff>

resolution.verification: - Update ConfigMap with new pool size - Restart pods to apply configuration - Monitor connection pool metrics - Verify no more timeout errors under load

example.name: n_plus_one_query_performance
example.title: N+1 Query Problem Causing Performance Degradation
example.scenario: Customer list endpoint extremely slow (10+ seconds). Database CPU high. Instana shows thousands of database calls per request.

phase_1_instana.title: Phase 1: Instana Analysis
phase_1_instana.findings: - /api/customers endpoint P99 latency: 12,000ms - Single request generates 1,000+ database calls - Each call fast (5-10ms) but volume is excessive - Pattern: 1 query for customers, then 1 query per customer for orders

phase_2_openshift.title: Phase 2: OpenShift Investigation
phase_2_openshift.findings: - Pods healthy, no crashes or restarts - CPU usage high during slow requests - Database logs show repeated similar queries

phase_3_code_analysis.title: Phase 3: Code Analysis
phase_3_code_analysis.issues_identified: Classic N+1 query problem: - 1 query to fetch all customers - N queries (one per customer) to fetch orders - With 1000 customers = 1001 total queries
phase_3_code_analysis.root_cause_confirmed: N+1 query anti-pattern in customer list endpoint. Each customer triggers separate query for orders instead of using JOIN or batch fetch.

immediate_fix.description: Use JOIN FETCH to load customers with orders in single query

resolution.verification: - Deploy fix - Verify single query in Instana traces - Confirm latency reduced to ~200ms - Monitor database CPU (should decrease significantly)

common_pattern.step: Start with Instana to identify symptoms and patterns
Use OpenShift to correlate with infrastructure events
Analyze code to find root cause
Form and validate hypotheses with evidence
Implement targeted fix addressing root cause

key_principles.principle: Always gather evidence from all three sources
Distinguish between symptoms and root causes
Validate fixes before considering incident resolved
